text: {"final": {"verdict": "reject", "reason": "The code contradicts the finding. notifications/sms.py has no send_sms(phone, text) function; the sending function is queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage, which takes a household ID plus a template ID and params, not a raw phone/text. MAX_LENGTH is 140, not 160. The appended record contains more keys than id/phone/text/queued_at — it also includes household_id, template_id, and params. The parts about checking feature('sms_enabled') and appending to outbox/sms.jsonl (which the gateway sends) are correct, but the function name, signature, limit, and record shape are wrong, so a script built on this finding would not work."}}
reasoning: The finding claims send_sms(phone, text, *, now=None) -> dict exists, checks feature('sms_enabled'), enforces len(text) <= MAX_LENGTH (160), builds record with keys id/phone/text/queued_at, appends to data/outbox/sms.jsonl. Actual code: no send_sms function; queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) exists; MAX_LENGTH is 140, not 160; record includes more keys (id, household_id, phone, template_id, params, text, queued_at).
